correctness.rationale: The proof normalizes by diameter, derives exact sector and parallel-body formulas, proves strict monotonicity of the rounded-equilateral scale invariant \(q=A/P^2\), identifies the exact unique zero of the perimeter-matched area defect, and then uses the intermediate-value theorem plus homothety to obtain equal perimeter and area with strictly smaller diameter. The critical formulas and representative roots are replayed by `verify.py`. The numerical replay is not used as proof of the continuum statement.

originality.rationale: The 2013 source proposes circular sectors as likely low-area minimizers. The closest modern full diagram treatment states that the exact classical lower boundary is known only up to normalized perimeter \(3\) and handles the continuation beyond \(3\) numerically; it does not state the rounded-equilateral threshold. The prescribed-perimeter/diameter theorem of Pan--Sun--Wang concerns the upper-area branch. Exact-form and implication-level searches found no covering statement.
residual_risks: An older unindexed source may contain the same explicit outer-parallel equilateral comparison under different terminology.

The classical lower-boundary literature predates modern indexing; the comparison against it relies in part on the scope characterization in the inspected 2025 diagram paper rather than direct inspection of every historical source.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a continuum of exact counterexamples to a published convex-geometric minimization proposal and gives a closed transition angle. Its strict part enters the normalized-perimeter-above-\(3\) region that the modern Blaschke--Santaló diagram literature still treats numerically. The competitor family is canonical, interpolating by outer parallel bodies from the equilateral triangle to the disk, and the result is stronger than a one-off numerical counterexample.
